title: Tooling defects found during the factory run
description:
Four defects in tk and the herd substrate, all found by RUNNING the factory epics rather than by testing them. Grouped so they get one review and one closeout instead of four ad-hoc fixes.

  201  herd dashboard truncates the epic list instead of scrolling it
  09w  tk herd collect boundary check conflates tracker state with project config
  5jo  herd agent names collide across repos (tick-<id> is a global namespace)
  3nh  support herdr protocol 20 (server auto-updated to 0.8.2 mid-run)

Common thread worth stating: each one is invisible to the test suite and only appears with a real multi-repo, multi-runner, live-server workload. 201 hides work from the operator, 09w trains the operator to wave through boundary violations, 5jo can silently bind one repo to another repos worker, and 3nh hard-stops every in-flight run when a background upgrade lands. They are ordinary bugs individually; together they are the difference between a demo and something you can leave running.

2026-08-22 12:26 - runner-state: substrate=harness requested=harness config=auto source=TICKS_SUBSTRATE reason=explicit-override

Recorded here by the epic-1vn orchestrator rather than by merging PR #52 or #53. Two cloud runs of this epic (run_1ce4fae5..., run_1f9e082a394840fcb539befb82ccdf45) each opened a closeout PR to main whose only content was this note, and each landed ZERO worker commits — because every per-tick worker container died at boot on exit 7 (EXIT_MODEL): the worker resolved [roles.implement] = sonnet -> provider anthropic, and the factory gateway routes workers-ai only. Tick ys3 owns that fix.

Both PRs are closed as superseded rather than merged: each would have carried ~107 unreviewed epic/1vn commits into main as a side effect (the hazard tick 6tt describes), to deliver two lines of tracker state. This epic will be re-run live as the evidence run for tick 5bv once ys3 and wiy land, and that run's PR is the one worth reviewing.

acceptance_criteria: The dashboard reaches every epic and tick on a roadmap taller than the viewport; a tick editing .tick/config.md or .tick/runners.toml collects clean while one editing tick state still fails closed; two repos sharing a tick id run concurrently without wait/collect/reconcile crossing between them; tk herd works against herdr 0.8.2 with internal/herd green and a documented compatibility policy.
